primitives.name: Non-Centered Parameterization
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Non-centered parameterization:** β_jt = β_j + √θ_j · β̃_jt with β̃_jt a standardized random walk.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\beta_{jt}': 'time-varying coefficient at time t for j-th predictor, dimensionless', '\\beta_j': 'mean coefficient, dimensionless', '\\theta_j': 'process variance for j-th coefficient, positive real', '\\tilde{\\beta}_{jt}': 'standardized random walk component, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Coefficients evolve via random walk; process variances are diagonal and non-negative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When θ_j → 0, the coefficient becomes static; when θ_j > 0, it varies stochastically.

layer2.mapping: Transforms variance selection problem into coefficient selection using shrinkage priors.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior inclusion probability of dynamic components.

primitives.name: Continuous Shrinkage Priors
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Priors on √θ_j: ridge/gamma, Bayesian Lasso, normal-gamma, double gamma, triple gamma, horseshoe, and discrete spike-and-slab with hierarchical Student-t / Gaussian / fractional slabs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\sqrt{\\theta}_j': 'square root of process variance, positive real', 'Shrinkage Prior': 'family of distributions inducing sparsity'}
primitives.assumptions: Process variances are shrunk toward zero; hierarchical structure allows local and global shrinkage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: All coefficients classified as zero under over-shrinking (e.g., Lasso).

layer2.mapping: Enables probabilistic classification of coefficients into zero/fixed/dynamic via thresholding.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior probability of dynamic behavior (1 − ρ_j > 0.5).

primitives.name: Spike-and-Slab Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Spike-and-slab: β_j | δ_j with point mass at 0 vs slab; second indicator γ_j for fixed vs dynamic.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\beta_j': 'coefficient value, dimensionless', '\\delta_j': 'binary indicator for zero (0) or slab (1), binary', '\\gamma_j': 'binary indicator for fixed (0) or dynamic (1), binary', '\\mu_j, \\sigma^2_j': 'mean and variance of slab distribution, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Each coefficient has a point mass at zero and a continuous slab; two-level classification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When δ_j = 1, β_j is non-zero; when γ_j = 0, β_j is fixed; otherwise dynamic.

layer2.mapping: Provides discrete classification of coefficients into zero/fixed/dynamic using binary indicators.
layer2.telemetry: Marginal posterior probabilities P(zero), P(fixed), P(dynamic).

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in transforming the hard variance selection problem (θ_j = 0?) into an easier coefficient selection task (√θ_j = 0?). The non-centered parameterization achieves this by reparameterizing β_jt = β_j + √θ_j · β̃_jt where β̃_jt is a standardized random walk. This enables the use of shrinkage priors on √θ_j, which naturally induce sparsity. Continuous shrinkage priors such as horseshoe or triple gamma allow for flexible modeling of the process variances, while discrete spike-and-slab priors provide hard classification into zero, fixed, or dynamic regimes. The MCMC algorithm uses forward-filtering backward-sampling (FFBS) for state estimation and ASIS to improve mixing. In GSE, these primitives enable adaptive team strength modeling where teams with high posterior probability of being dynamic receive time-varying ratings, while others remain static. The failure mode occurs when Lasso-like priors over-shrink all coefficients, misclassifying them as zero.
